Title: Choco-solver: A Java library for constraint programming
Summary: Constraint Programming (CP) is a powerful paradigm for combinatorial search problems. This JOSS paper documents Choco-solver as a Java CP library and is the cleanest citation for the solver backend used throughout your report.

Title: CSPLIB: A Benchmark Library for Constraints
Summary: CSPLib was created as a benchmark library for constraint problems. The paper stresses diversity, extensibility, and solver-independence, which fits your benchmark-suite discussion.

Title: CSPLib: Twenty Years On
Summary: This follow-up revisits CSPLib after twenty years and explains why natural-language benchmark descriptions still matter. It is a good citation for your remarks about representation and benchmarking in constraint programming.

Title: PYCSP3: Modeling Combinatorial Constrained Problems in Python
Summary: PyCSP3 is a Python modelling library that cleanly separates model construction from solving. It is useful as a citation for the modeling/solving split, even if you keep Choco as the concrete backend.

Title: Is Neuro-Symbolic AI Meeting its Promise in Natural Language Processing? A Structured Review
Authors: Kyle Hamilton, Aparna Nayak, Bojan Bozic, Longo Luca
Summary: This structured review asks whether neuro-symbolic AI is meeting its promises in NLP, focusing on reasoning, out-of-distribution generalization, interpretability, learning from small data, and transfer to new domains. It fits your section defining neuro-symbolic systems and why they are attractive.

Title: Prompt2DeModel: Declarative Neuro-Symbolic Modeling with Natural Language
Authors: Hossein Rajaby Faghihi, Aliakbar Nafar, Andrzej Uszok, Hamid Karimian, Parisa Kordjamshidi
Summary: Prompt2DeModel uses large language models to generate declarative programs from natural language prompts. It is a strong modern reference for the NL-to-symbolic-model pipeline that sits closest to your task.

Title: Chain of Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
Authors: Jason Wei, Xuezhi Wang, Dale Schuurmans, Maarten Bosma, Ed H. Chi, F. Xia, Quoc Le, Denny Zhou
Summary: This paper shows that chain-of-thought prompting can significantly improve complex reasoning in LLMs, including symbolic tasks. It supports your section on prompting families and the case for reasoning traces.

Title: Iteratively Prompt Pre-trained Language Models for Chain of Thought
Authors: Boshi Wang, Xiang Deng, Huan Sun
Summary: This paper proposes an iterative prompting framework that dynamically synthesizes prompts conditioned on the current reasoning step. It is a good citation for any discussion of iterative refinement or staged prompting.

Title: AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation
Authors: Qingyun Wu, Gagan Bansal, Jieyu Zhang, Yiran Wu, Beibin Li, E. Zhu, Li Jiang, Xiaoyun Zhang, Shaokun Zhang, Jiale Liu, A. Awadallah, Ryen W. White, D. Burger, Chi Wang
Summary: AutoGen is a multi-agent conversation framework for building LLM applications with customizable agents, human inputs, and tools. It is the natural citation when you compare single-agent and multi-agent orchestration.

Title: MetaGPT: Meta Programming for Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework
Authors: Sirui Hong, Xiawu Zheng, Jonathan P. Chen, Yuheng Cheng, Ceyao Zhang, Zili Wang, Steven Ka Shing Yau, Z. Lin, Liyang Zhou, Chenyu Ran, Lingfeng Xiao, Chenglin Wu
Summary: MetaGPT encodes human workflows as a multi-agent meta-programming approach and reports better coherence and correctness on collaborative software-engineering tasks. It fits your argument about role specialization and cascading hallucinations.

Title: ChatDev: Communicative Agents for Software Development
Authors: Cheng Qian, Wei Liu, Hongzhang Liu, Nuo Chen, Yufan Dang, Jiahao Li, Cheng Yang, Weize Chen, Yusheng Su, X. Cong, Juyuan Xu, Dahai Li, Zhiyuan Liu, Maosong Sun
Summary: ChatDev is a chat-powered software-development framework with specialized agents that communicate through a chat chain and communicative dehallucination. It is a good second citation alongside AutoGen and MetaGPT.

Title: Towards Cognitive AI Systems: a Survey and Prospective on Neuro-Symbolic AI
Authors: Zishen Wan, Che-Kai Liu, Hanchen Yang, Chaojian Li, Haoran You, Yonggan Fu, Cheng Wan, Tushar Krishna, Y. Lin, A. Raychowdhury
Summary: Neuro-symbolic AI is presented as a promising paradigm that fuses neural, symbolic, and probabilistic approaches to improve interpretability, robustness, and trustworthiness. It is a useful broader survey citation for the motivation section and discussion of system-level tradeoffs.
